thread:
mia (support): heads up — ACME (acme-marketing) just escalated: p95 ~600ms -> p99 ~2.4s on /v1/generate since ~2026-03-16 22:10 UTC. They say it started after last night's driver/CUDA rollout. req id example: req-9a8b. Can we triage?

jia (oncall-sre): ack. pinging eng-runtime + infra. can you paste a few request ids and tenant/region? I’ll pull traces.

mia (support): reqs: req-9a8b, req-c3f2, req-77aa. tenant acme-marketing, region: us-west-2 (hosted-api). Customer reporting SLO breaches.

infra-bot: [alert] cluster-usw2-pool-7 p99 > 2s; NVMe qdepth high; KV cache miss rate spike. link: https://telemetry/redwood/alerts/1778003456

sasha (eng-runtime): looking at traces — KV cache thrash on small-batch embed requests + host IO tail. nvme %util jumps, queue_depth spikes from ~32 -> 512 after CUDA/driver rollout. reproduces with small-batch (batch_size 1-4) embed workload.

ravi (eng-infra): if NVMe qdepth jumped that high we might be hitting a driver change that exposes different queueing defaults. Options: 1) immediate route ACME to older nodepool/dedicated capacity 2) throttle client retry/backoff 3) quick host qdepth tune to cap nr_requests 4) rollback driver on a canary subset. Thoughts?

mia (support): customer needs ETA — prefer minimal blast radius. Can we route them to dedicated pool while we investigate? they accepted temporary fallback.

sasha (eng-runtime): I can flip per-host qdepth to 64 for affected hosts as a stopgap. command I’ll run:

```bash
for h in $(cat affected_hosts.txt); do
  ssh $h "echo 64 > /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/nr_requests"
done
```

That reduces outstanding IO and KV cache eviction pressure.

ravi (eng-infra): I'll prepare driver rollback on 10-node canary (non-prod -> prod staged). rollback script: rollout-driver --rollback --group canary-2 --wait 5m. doing a controlled rollback seems safer than kernel hotpatch.

jia (oncall-sre): traces show auth service also experienced increased latency (auth retries + timeouts), adding to end-to-end. I'll add retry-throttle rule at edge for tenant acme-marketing to avoid amplifying load.

mia (support): applied routing to dedicated pool + edge retry throttle. customer reports slightly improved but still sees occasional tails. Keeping them updated. :pray:

sasha (eng-runtime): applied qdepth tweak on 8 hosts hitting that tenant. p95 dropped from ~600ms to ~260ms within 6m, p99 down to ~700ms. KV miss rate fell ~40%.

deploy-bot: driver-rollback job started on canary-2 (nodes 2/10) — see CI job 5771.

ravi (eng-infra): started rollback on canary. so far no regressions in throughput. If canary looks good we'll continue roll forward in 10-node steps.

jia (oncall-sre): auth retry throttle + qdepth tweak + routing look to have stabilized customer metrics. collecting dmesg/nvme smart/logs for postmortem. Please gather: nvme_iostat, dmesg, kernel sched traces, driver version strings, telemetry snapshots for last 24h.

sasha (eng-runtime): collecting perf counters now. saved snapshot to s3://redwood-telemetry/1778003456-acme-kv-qdepth.

mia (support): ACME confirms latency back within SLO on their side after being routed to dedicated pool. They accepted temporary mitigation and asked for root cause and plan.

ravi (eng-infra): next actions: 1) continue rollback on remaining canaries if no regressions 2) open vendor ticket with driver/CUDA vendor (attach telemetry) 3) run focused replay tests for small-batch embed patterns on new driver 4) consider permanent qdepth tuning or autoscale knob for KV-cache heavy tenants.

sasha (eng-runtime): agree. long-term: improve KV cache pressure logging, add anomaly alerting for small-batch embed patterns, and consider local batching suggestion at SDK for high-cardinality tenants.

infra-bot: [note] saved incident snapshot and kicked postmortem template -> PM-INC-1778003456.

mia (support): customer notified. closing escalation channel after PM created. thanks team. :thumbsup:

jia (oncall-sre): assigning postmortem owners: sasha (eng-runtime), ravi (eng-infra). leaving oncall notes in pagerduty.

sasha (eng-runtime): ACK. I’ll attach reproduction steps and the small-batch replay script to the postmortem.

mia (support): closing thread — customer happy with mitigation for now, PM will follow with RCAs and long-term mitigations.
